sanskrit: yadā śikhaṇḍī rathinaḥ pracinvan; bhīṣmaṃ rathenābhiyātā varūthī divyair hayair avamṛdnan rathaughāṃs; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When Śikhaṇḍī, a chariot-fighter advancing against Bhīṣma in his chariot, fully armored, crushes the enemy's chariot-masses with celestial horses — then Dhārtarāṣṭra will repent of the war.

sanskrit: yadā draṣṭā sṛñjayānām anīke; dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ pramukhe rocamānam astraṃ yasmai guhyam uvāca dhīmān; droṇas tadā tapsyati dhārtarāṣṭraḥ
english: When he sees Dhṛṣṭadyumna shining at the forefront of the Sṛñjaya army — he to whom the wise Droṇa taught his secret weapon — then Dhārtarāṣṭra will repent.

sanskrit: yadā sa senāpatir aprameyaḥ; parābhavann iṣubhir dhārtarāṣṭrān droṇaṃ raṇe śatrusaho 'bhiyātā; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When that immeasurable commander, overwhelming the Dhārtarāṣṭras with his arrows, advances against Droṇa in battle, bearing down on his foe — then Dhārtarāṣṭra will repent of the war.

sanskrit: hrīmān manīṣī balavān manasvī; sa lakṣmīvān somakānāṃ prabarhaḥ na jātu taṃ śatravo 'nye saheran; yeṣāṃ sa syād agraṇīr vṛṣṇisiṃhaḥ
english: He is modest, wise, strong, and resolute — endowed with fortune, the foremost among the Somakas. No other enemies could ever endure him, if that lion of the Vṛṣṇis were to lead them.

sanskrit: brūyāc ca mā pravṛṇīṣveti loke; yuddhe 'dvitīyaṃ sacivaṃ rathastham śiner naptāraṃ pravṛṇīma sātyakiṃ; mahābalaṃ vītabhayaṃ kṛtāstram
english: Though the world might say 'do not choose him,' we choose Sātyaki, the grandson of Śini, as our unrivaled ally on the chariot in battle — mighty, fearless, and skilled in arms.

sanskrit: yadā śinīnām adhipo mayoktaḥ; śaraiḥ parān megha iva pravarṣan pracchādayiṣyañ śarajālena yodhāṃs; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When the lord of the Śinis, as commanded by me, rains arrows on the foe like a cloud pouring rain and covers the warriors in a net of shafts — then Dhārtarāṣṭra will repent of the war.

sanskrit: yadā dhṛtiṃ kurute yotsyamānaḥ; sa dīrghabāhur dṛḍhadhanvā mahātmā siṃhasyeva gandham āghrāya gāvaḥ; saṃveṣṭante śatravo 'smād yathāgneḥ
english: When that long-armed, firm-bowed great soul girds himself for battle, enemies shrink away from him as cattle scatter on smelling a lion, and as from fire.

sanskrit: sa dīrghabāhur dṛḍhadhanvā mahātmā; bhindyād girīn saṃharet sarvalokān astre kṛtī nipuṇaḥ kṣiprahasto; divi sthitaḥ sūrya ivābhibhāti
english: That long-armed, firm-bowed great soul could cleave mountains and destroy all worlds; expert in weapons, skillful, swift-handed — he blazes in the sky like the sun.

sanskrit: citraḥ sūkṣmaḥ sukṛto yādavasya; astre yogo vṛṣṇisiṃhasya bhūyān yathāvidhaṃ yogam āhuḥ praśastaṃ; sarvair guṇaiḥ sātyakis tair upetaḥ
english: The mastery in arms of the lion of the Vṛṣṇis — the Yādava — is varied, subtle, and well-wrought. Just as they speak of the highest discipline perfected in every virtue, so Sātyaki is endowed with all those qualities.

sanskrit: hiraṇmayaṃ śvetahayaiś caturbhir; yadā yuktaṃ syandanaṃ mādhavasya draṣṭā yuddhe sātyaker vai suyodhanas; tadā tapsyaty akṛtātmā sa mandaḥ
english: When Suyodhana sees in battle the golden chariot of Mādhava yoked with four white horses — and sees Sātyaki — then that foolish, unrestrained man will repent.

sanskrit: yadā rathaṃ hemamaṇiprakāśaṃ; śvetāśvayuktaṃ vānaraketum ugram draṣṭā raṇe saṃyataṃ keśavena; tadā tapsyaty akṛtātmā sa mandaḥ
english: When he sees in battle the chariot gleaming with gold and jewels, yoked with white horses, bearing the terrible monkey-banner, governed by Keśava — then that foolish, unrestrained man will repent.

sanskrit: yadā maurvyās talaniṣpeṣam ugraṃ; mahāśabdaṃ vajraniṣpeṣatulyam vidhūyamānasya mahāraṇe mayā; gāṇḍīvasya śroṣyati mandabuddhiḥ
english: When that dull-witted one hears the terrible, thunderous slap of the bowstring against my palm as I brandish the Gāṇḍīva in the great battle — a sound equal to the crash of the thunderbolt —

sanskrit: tadā mūḍho dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putras; taptā yuddhe durmatir duḥsahāyaḥ dṛṣṭvā sainyaṃ bāṇavarṣāndhakāraṃ; prabhajyantaṃ gokulavad raṇāgre
english: — then that foolish son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that evil-minded one with wretched allies, will be scorched in battle as he watches his army scatter like a herd of cattle before a rain-darkness of arrows at the battle's front.

sanskrit: balāhakād uccarantīva vidyut; sahasraghnī dviṣatāṃ saṃgameṣu asthicchido marmabhido vamec charāṃs; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: Rising like lightning from a thundercloud, slaying thousands of foes in their midst, I will pour forth bone-piercing, vital-point-splitting arrows — then Dhārtarāṣṭra will repent of the war.

sanskrit: yadā draṣṭā jyāmukhād bāṇasaṃghān; gāṇḍīvamuktān patataḥ śitāgrān nāgān hayān varmiṇaś cādadānāṃs; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When he sees the multitudes of sharp-tipped arrows loosed from the mouth of the Gāṇḍīva's string swooping down to take elephants, horses, and armored warriors — then Dhārtarāṣṭra will repent of the war.

sanskrit: yadā mandaḥ parabāṇān vimuktān; mameṣubhir hriyamāṇān pratīpam tiryag vidvāṃś chidyamānān kṣuraprais; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When that dullard sees the enemy's released arrows being carried back against their course and cut crosswise, being intercepted and severed by my razor-headed shafts — then Dhārtarāṣṭra will repent of the war.

sanskrit: yadā vipāṭhā madbhujavipramuktā; dvijāḥ phalānīva mahīruhāgrāt pracchettāra uttamāṅgāni yūnāṃ; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When the broad-bladed arrows released from my arm, like birds from a treetop, sever the heads of young warriors — then Dhārtarāṣṭra will repent of the war.

sanskrit: yadā draṣṭā patataḥ syandanebhyo; mahāgajebhyo 'śvagatāṃś ca yodhān śarair hatān pātitāṃś caiva raṅge; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When he sees warriors struck by arrows falling from their chariots, from great elephants, and from horses, and brought down on the arena of battle — then Dhārtarāṣṭra will repent of the war.

sanskrit: padātisaṃghān rathasaṃghān samantād; vyāttānanaḥ kāla ivātateṣuḥ praṇotsyāmi jvalitair bāṇavarṣaiḥ; śatrūṃs tadā tapsyati mandabuddhiḥ
english: Like Death with his mouth agape and his bow drawn, I will drive off masses of infantry and masses of chariots on all sides with blazing showers of arrows against the enemy — then the dull-witted one will repent.

sanskrit: sarvā diśaḥ saṃpatatā rathena; rajodhvastaṃ gāṇḍivenāpakṛttam yadā draṣṭā svabalaṃ saṃpramūḍhaṃ; tadā paścāt tapsyati mandabuddhiḥ
english: When, as I range across all directions with my chariot, he sees his own army bewildered and cut down by the Gāṇḍīva, overwhelmed by dust — then afterward that dull-witted one will repent.

sanskrit: kāṃdigbhūtaṃ chinnagātraṃ visaṃjñaṃ; duryodhano drakṣyati sarvasainyam hatāśvavīrāgryanarendranāgaṃ; pipāsitaṃ śrāntapatraṃ bhayārtam
english: Duryodhana will see his entire army maddened, its limbs severed, unconscious, with its foremost horses, heroes, men, and elephants slain — thirsty, its wings broken, afflicted with fear.

sanskrit: ārtasvaraṃ hanyamānaṃ hataṃ ca; vikīrṇakeśāsthikapālasaṃgham prajāpateḥ karma yathārdhaniṣṭhitaṃ; tadā dṛṣṭvā tapsyate mandabuddhiḥ
english: Crying out in agony, being slaughtered and slain, the army will be strewn with scattered hair, bones, and skulls, as if Prajāpati's work had been left half-done — seeing this, the dull-witted one will repent.

sanskrit: yadā rathe gāṇḍivaṃ vāsudevaṃ; divyaṃ śaṅkhaṃ pāñcajanyaṃ hayāṃś ca tūṇāv akṣayyau devadattaṃ ca māṃ ca; draṣṭā yuddhe dhārtarāṣṭraḥ sametān
english: When Dhārtarāṣṭra sees gathered on the chariot in battle: the Gāṇḍīva, Vāsudeva, the divine conch Pāñcajanya, the horses, the two inexhaustible quivers, Devadatta, and me —

sanskrit: udvartayan dasyusaṃghān sametān; pravartayan yugam anyad yugānte yadā dhakṣyāmy agnivat kauraveyāṃs; tadā taptā dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saputraḥ
english: — when at the end of the age I shall burn the Kauravas like fire, routing the assembled bands of plunderers and ushering in a new age — then Dhṛtarāṣṭra along with his son will be scorched.

sanskrit: sahabhrātā sahaputraḥ sasainyo; bhraṣṭaiśvaryaḥ krodhavaśo 'lpacetāḥ darpasyānte vihite vepamānaḥ; paścān mandas tapsyati dhārtarāṣṭraḥ
english: Together with his brothers, together with his son, together with his army, bereft of sovereignty, a slave to anger, of small intelligence — trembling at the end of his pride when it has been ordained — that fool Dhārtarāṣṭra will afterward repent.

sanskrit: pūrvāhṇe māṃ kṛtajapyaṃ kadā cid; vipraḥ provācodakānte manojñam kartavyaṃ te duṣkaraṃ karma pārtha; yoddhavyaṃ te śatrubhiḥ savyasācin
english: Once at dawn, after I had completed my recitations, a brahmin spoke to me pleasantly at the water's edge: 'O Pārtha, a hard task is appointed for you — you must fight against your enemies, O Savyasācin.'

sanskrit: indro vā te harivān vajrahastaḥ; purastād yātu samare 'rīn vinighnan sugrīvayuktena rathena vā te; paścāt kṛṣṇo rakṣatu vāsudevaḥ
english: 'May Indra, the thunderbolt-wielder with the tawny horses, go before you in battle, slaying your enemies; and may Kṛṣṇa Vāsudeva protect you from behind, on your chariot yoked with Sugrīva.'

sanskrit: vavre cāhaṃ vajrahastān mahendrād; asmin yuddhe vāsudevaṃ sahāyam sa me labdho dasyuvadhāya kṛṣṇo; manye caitad vihitaṃ daivatair me
english: I chose Vāsudeva as my ally in this war from Mahendra, the thunderbolt-wielder. That Kṛṣṇa has been granted to me for the slaying of the plunderers — I deem this ordained for me by the gods.

sanskrit: ayudhyamāno manasāpi yasya; jayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ puruṣasyābhinandet dhruvaṃ sarvān so 'bhyatīyād amitrān; sendrān devān mānuṣe nāsti cintā
english: He in whose victory Kṛṣṇa rejoices even in his mind, without himself fighting — that man will certainly overcome all his enemies; of gods led by Indra there is no concern in the human world.

sanskrit: sa bāhubhyāṃ sāgaram uttitīrṣen; mahodadhiṃ salilasyāprameyam tejasvinaṃ kṛṣṇam atyantaśūraṃ; yuddhena yo vāsudevaṃ jigīṣet
english: He who wishes to defeat Vāsudeva Kṛṣṇa — so splendid, so utterly heroic — in battle would be trying to cross the great ocean, the immeasurable mass of waters, with his bare arms.

sanskrit: giriṃ ya iccheta talena bhettuṃ; śiloccayaṃ śvetam atipramāṇam tasyaiva pāṇiḥ sanakho viśīryen; na cāpi kiṃ cit sa gires tu kuryāt
english: He who wishes to split a mountain — that immense white mass of rock — with his palm: his own hand, nails and all, would crumble, and he would do nothing at all to the mountain.

sanskrit: agniṃ samiddhaṃ śamayed bhujābhyāṃ; candraṃ ca sūryaṃ ca nivārayeta hared devānām amṛtaṃ prasahya; yuddhena yo vāsudevaṃ jigīṣet
english: He who wishes to defeat Vāsudeva in battle would be trying to quench a blazing fire with his arms, to stop the moon and sun in their courses, and to seize by force the immortal nectar of the gods.

sanskrit: yo rukmiṇīm ekarathena bhojyām; utsādya rājñāṃ viṣayaṃ prasahya uvāha bhāryāṃ yaśasā jvalantīṃ; yasyāṃ jajñe raukmiṇeyo mahātmā
english: He who, on a single chariot, overwhelmed the Bhoja kings and forcibly seized their territory, then carried off as his wife Rukmiṇī blazing with glory — from whom the great-souled son of Rukmiṇī was born —

sanskrit: ayaṃ gāndhārāṃs tarasā saṃpramathya; jitvā putrān nagnajitaḥ samagrān baddhaṃ mumoca vinadantaṃ prasahya; sudarśanīyaṃ devatānāṃ lalāmam
english: He swiftly crushed the Gāndhāras and conquered all the sons of Nagnajit; forcibly releasing, bellowing, the one who had been bound — that jewel of the gods, fair to behold.

sanskrit: ayaṃ kavāṭe nijaghāna pāṇḍyaṃ; tathā kaliṅgān dantakūre mamarda anena dagdhā varṣapūgān vināthā; vārāṇasī nagarī saṃbabhūva
english: He slew the Pāṇḍya at Kavāṭa and crushed the Kaliṅgas at Dantakūra. By him was the city of Vārāṇasī burned, rendered masterless for many long years.

sanskrit: yaṃ sma yuddhe manyate 'nyair ajeyam; ekalavyaṃ nāma niṣādarājam vegeneva śailam abhihatya jambhaḥ; śete sa kṛṣṇena hataḥ parāsuḥ
english: Ekalavya, the Niṣāda king whom others deemed unconquerable in battle — he lies dead, slain by Kṛṣṇa who struck him like Jambha striking a mountain with speed.

sanskrit: tathograsenasya sutaṃ praduṣṭaṃ; vṛṣṇyandhakānāṃ madhyagāṃ tapantam apātayad baladevadvitīyo; hatvā dadau cograsenāya rājyam
english: Likewise the wicked son of Ugrasena, who oppressed the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas in their midst — he felled him, together with Baladeva, and having slain him gave the kingdom to Ugrasena.

sanskrit: ayaṃ saubhaṃ yodhayām āsa khasthaṃ; vibhīṣaṇaṃ māyayā śālvarājam saubhadvāri pratyagṛhṇāc chataghnīṃ; dorbhyāṃ ka enaṃ viṣaheta martyaḥ
english: He battled the flying city Saubha, and through his illusion-power struck down Śālva the terrible. At the gate of Saubha he caught the śataghni with his bare arms. What mortal could endure him?

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣaṃ nāma babhūva durgaṃ; puraṃ ghoram asurāṇām asahyam mahābalo narakas tatra bhaumo; jahārādityā maṇikuṇḍale śubhe
english: There was a fortress called Prāgjyotiṣa, a terrible city of the demons, impossible to storm. There the mighty Naraka, son of Earth, stole the beautiful jeweled earrings from the Ādityas.

sanskrit: na taṃ devāḥ saha śakreṇa sehire; samāgatā āharaṇāya bhītāḥ dṛṣṭvā ca te vikramaṃ keśavasya; balaṃ tathaivāstram avāraṇīyam
english: The gods assembled with Indra could not endure him and were afraid to retrieve the earrings. But when they saw the prowess of Keśava — his irresistible strength and weaponry —

sanskrit: jānanto 'sya prakṛtiṃ keśavasya; nyayojayan dasyuvadhāya kṛṣṇam sa tat karma pratiśuśrāva duṣkaram; aiśvaryavān siddhiṣu vāsudevaḥ
english: — knowing the nature of Keśava, they commissioned Kṛṣṇa for the slaying of the plunderer. He, Vāsudeva — sovereign in his accomplishments — undertook that difficult task.

sanskrit: nirmocane ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi hatvā; saṃchidya pāśān sahasā kṣurāntān muraṃ hatvā vinihatyaugharākṣasaṃ; nirmocanaṃ cāpi jagāma vīraḥ
english: At Nirmocana he slew six thousand, instantly cutting through the razor-edged snares. Having killed Mura and slaughtered Ogha the demon, the hero went on to Nirmocana.

sanskrit: tatraiva tenāsya babhūva yuddhaṃ; mahābalenātibalasya viṣṇoḥ śete sa kṛṣṇena hataḥ parāsur; vāteneva mathitaḥ karṇikāraḥ
english: Right there a battle took place between him and Viṣṇu of surpassing might. He lies dead, slain by Kṛṣṇa, like a karṇikāra tree knocked down by the wind.

sanskrit: āhṛtya kṛṣṇo maṇikuṇḍale te; hatvā ca bhaumaṃ narakaṃ muraṃ ca śriyā vṛto yaśasā caiva dhīmān; pratyājagāmāpratimaprabhāvaḥ
english: Having retrieved those jeweled earrings, and having slain Bhauma Naraka and Mura, the wise one, attended by Śrī and by glory, returned — he of matchless majesty.

sanskrit: tasmai varān adadaṃs tatra devā; dṛṣṭvā bhīmaṃ karma raṇe kṛtaṃ tat śramaś ca te yudhyamānasya na syād; ākāśe vā apsu caiva kramaḥ syāt
english: The gods there bestowed boons upon him, having witnessed that tremendous feat accomplished in battle: 'May you feel no fatigue when fighting; may you walk freely in the sky and in the waters.'

sanskrit: śastrāṇi gātre ca na te kramerann; ity eva kṛṣṇaś ca tataḥ kṛtārthaḥ evaṃrūpe vāsudeve 'prameye; mahābale guṇasaṃpat sadaiva
english: 'And may weapons find no purchase on your body.' Thus Kṛṣṇa was there fulfilled in his purpose. In Vāsudeva, immeasurable and of great might, the fullness of virtue is ever present.

sanskrit: tam asahyaṃ viṣṇum anantavīryam; āśaṃsate dhārtarāṣṭro balena yadā hy enaṃ tarkayate durātmā; tac cāpy ayaṃ sahate 'smān samīkṣya
english: Dhārtarāṣṭra believes he can overcome with force that unendurable Viṣṇu of boundless valor — yet when that evil-souled one reasons about him, he tolerates even that and looks upon us.

sanskrit: paryāgataṃ mama kṛṣṇasya caiva; yo manyate kalahaṃ saṃprayujya śakyaṃ hartuṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mamatvaṃ; tad veditā saṃyugaṃ tatra gatvā
english: Whoever thinks that by picking a quarrel with Kṛṣṇa and me in our combined strength it is possible to deprive the Pāṇḍavas of what is theirs — let him go there and find out in the clash of battle.

sanskrit: namaskṛtvā śāṃtanavāya rājñe; droṇāyātho sahaputrāya caiva śāradvatāyāpratidvandvine ca; yotsyāmy ahaṃ rājyam abhīpsamānaḥ
english: Having paid homage to King Śāntanava, and likewise to Droṇa together with his son, and to Śāradvatī who has no equal in combat — I will fight, desiring the kingdom.

sanskrit: dharmeṇāstraṃ niyataṃ tasya manye; yo yotsyate pāṇḍavair dharmacārī mithyāglahe nirjitā vai nṛśaṃsaiḥ; saṃvatsarān dvādaśa pāṇḍuputrāḥ
english: I deem the weapons destined by righteousness for the one who will fight the Pāṇḍavas in accordance with dharma. The sons of Pāṇḍu were defeated in a fraudulent game by cruel men and spent twelve years in exile.

sanskrit: avāpya kṛcchraṃ vihitaṃ hy araṇye; dīrghaṃ kālaṃ caikam ajñātacaryām te hy akasmāj jīvitaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ; na mṛṣyante dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ padasthāḥ
english: Having endured the ordained hardship in the forest for a long time, and one year of living incognito — the Dhārtarāṣṭras, now firmly established, cannot suddenly tolerate the lives of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: te ced asmān yudhyamānāñ jayeyur; devair apīndrapramukhaiḥ sahāyaiḥ dharmād adharmaś carito garīyān; iti dhruvaṃ nāsti kṛtaṃ na sādhu
english: If they were to defeat us in battle even with gods led by Indra as allies, then adharma practiced would outweigh dharma — that is certain; nothing done would be good.

sanskrit: na ced imaṃ puruṣaṃ karmabaddhaṃ; na ced asmān manyate 'sau viśiṣṭān āśaṃse 'haṃ vāsudevadvitīyo; duryodhanaṃ sānubandhaṃ nihantum
english: If this man is not bound by his actions, if he does not deem us superior — I, together with Vāsudeva, expect to slay Duryodhana along with all his kin.

sanskrit: na ced idaṃ karma nareṣu baddhaṃ; na vidyate puruṣasya svakarma idaṃ ca tac cāpi samīkṣya nūnaṃ; parājayo dhārtarāṣṭrasya sādhuḥ
english: And if action is not ordained among men, if one's own karma does not exist for a person — then reflecting on both these arguments, the defeat of Dhārtarāṣṭra is surely right.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ vaḥ kuravo yad bravīmi; yudhyamānā dhārtarāṣṭrā na santi anyatra yuddhāt kuravaḥ parīpsan; na yudhyatāṃ śeṣa ihāsti kaś cit
english: O Kurus, what I declare to you is plain: the Dhārtarāṣṭras will not survive the fighting. The Kurus will not attain what they seek by any means other than battle; there is no survivor for those who refuse to fight here.

sanskrit: hatvā tv ahaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrān sakarṇān; rājyaṃ kurūṇām avajetā samagram yad vaḥ kāryaṃ tat kurudhvaṃ yathāsvam; iṣṭān dārān ātmajāṃś copabhuṅkta
english: But I, having slain the Dhārtarāṣṭras along with Karṇa, will win back the entire kingdom of the Kurus. Do each of you what must be done; enjoy your beloved wives and children.

sanskrit: apy evaṃ no brāhmaṇāḥ santi vṛddhā; bahuśrutāḥ śīlavantaḥ kulīnāḥ sāṃvatsarā jyotiṣi cāpi yuktā; nakṣatrayogeṣu ca niścayajñāḥ
english: Moreover, we have among us aged brahmins who are widely learned, of good character, and of noble lineage — yearly astronomers skilled in astrology, and knowers of the decisive configurations of the asterisms.

sanskrit: uccāvacaṃ daivayuktaṃ rahasyaṃ; divyāḥ praśnā mṛgacakrā muhūrtāḥ kṣayaṃ mahāntaṃ kurusṛñjayānāṃ; nivedayante pāṇḍavānāṃ jayaṃ ca
english: The high and the low ordained by fate, the divine questions, the MṛgaCakra, the auspicious hours — all of these declare a great destruction for the Kurus and Sṛñjayas, and victory for the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tathā hi no manyate 'jātaśatruḥ; saṃsiddhārtho dviṣatāṃ nigrahāya janārdanaś cāpy aparokṣavidyo; na saṃśayaṃ paśyati vṛṣṇisiṃhaḥ
english: Thus does Ajātaśatru think of us — his purpose accomplished, ready to suppress the enemy. And Janārdana, who knows things not hidden from him, the lion of the Vṛṣṇis sees no doubt in this.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca jānāmi bhaviṣyarūpaṃ; paśyāmi buddhyā svayam apramattaḥ dṛṣṭiś ca me na vyathate purāṇī; yudhyamānā dhārtarāṣṭrā na santi
english: And I too know the shape of what is to come; I see it with my own clear-eyed intelligence, ever vigilant. My ancient sight does not waver: the Dhārtarāṣṭras will not survive the battle.

sanskrit: anālabdhaṃ jṛmbhati gāṇḍivaṃ dhanur; anālabdhā kampati me dhanurjyā bāṇāś ca me tūṇamukhād visṛjya; muhur muhur gantum uśanti caiva
english: Without being touched, the Gāṇḍīva bow yawns open; without being touched, my bowstring quivers; and my arrows, springing themselves from the mouths of the quivers, yearn again and again to fly.

sanskrit: saikyaḥ kośān niḥsarati prasanno; hitveva jīrṇām uragas tvacaṃ svām dhvaje vāco raudrarūpā vadanti; kadā ratho yokṣyate te kirīṭin
english: My sword emerges brightly from its scabbard, as if a snake shedding its old skin. Voices of fearsome aspect speak from the banner: 'When will your chariot be yoked, O Crowned One?'

sanskrit: gomāyusaṃghāś ca vadanti rātrau; rakṣāṃsy atho niṣpatanty antarikṣāt mṛgāḥ śṛgālāḥ śitikaṇṭhāś ca kākā; gṛdhrā baḍāś caiva tarakṣavaś ca
english: Packs of jackals cry out in the night; demons spring down from the sky; deer and jackals, blue-necked peacocks and crows, vultures, herons, and hyenas —

sanskrit: suparṇapātāś ca patanti paścād; dṛṣṭvā rathaṃ śvetahayaprayuktam ahaṃ hy ekaḥ pārthivān sarvayodhāñ; śarān varṣan mṛtyulokaṃ nayeyam
english: — and Suparṇas descend and circle behind, as they observe my chariot yoked with white horses. For I alone, raining arrows, could lead all the earthly warriors to the realm of Death.

sanskrit: samādadānaḥ pṛthag astramārgān; yathāgnir iddho gahanaṃ nidāghe sthūṇākarṇaṃ pāśupataṃ ca ghoraṃ; tathā brahmāstraṃ yac ca śakro viveda
english: Drawing upon different paths of weaponry — like fire blazing through a thicket in the dry season — the Sthūṇākarṇa, the terrible Pāśupata, and the Brahmāstra that Indra himself knows:

sanskrit: vadhe dhṛto vegavataḥ pramuñcan; nāhaṃ prajāḥ kiṃ cid ivāvaśiṣye śāntiṃ lapsye paramo hy eṣa bhāvaḥ; sthiro mama brūhi gāvalgaṇe tān
english: — bent on slaughter, releasing them swiftly, I would leave scarcely any people remaining. I will attain peace — for that is the highest state, and this is my firm resolve. O son of Gavalgaṇa, tell them this.

sanskrit: nityaṃ punaḥ sacivair yair avocad; devān apīndrapramukhān sahāyān tair manyate kalahaṃ saṃprayujya; sa dhārtarāṣṭraḥ paśyata moham asya
english: He who was constantly counseled again and again by those ministers, and yet believes he can pick a quarrel with the gods led by Indra as his allies — that is Dhārtarāṣṭra. Behold his delusion.

sanskrit: vṛddho bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavaḥ kṛpaś ca; droṇaḥ saputro viduraś ca dhīmān ete sarve yad vadante tad astu; āyuṣmantaḥ kuravaḥ santu sarve
english: The aged Bhīṣma son of Śaṃtanu, and Kṛpa, and Droṇa together with his son, and the wise Vidura — may whatever all of them say come to pass. May all the Kurus live long.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca samaveteṣu sarveṣu teṣu rājasu bhārata duryodhanam idaṃ vākyaṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'bravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: O descendant of Bharata, when all those kings had assembled, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu spoke these words to Duryodhana.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatiś cośanā ca brahmāṇaṃ paryupasthitau marutaś ca sahendreṇa vasavaś ca sahāśvinau
english: Bṛhaspati and Uśanā had drawn near to Brahmā, and the Maruts together with Indra, and the Vasus together with the Aśvins.

sanskrit: ādityāś caiva sādhyāś ca ye ca saptarṣayo divi viśvāvasuś ca gandharvaḥ śubhāś cāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: The Ādityas, the Sādhyas, and the seven sages in heaven, Viśvāvasu the gandharva, and the lovely hosts of apsarases —

sanskrit: namaskṛtvopajagmus te lokavṛddhaṃ pitāmaham parivārya ca viśveśaṃ paryāsata divaukasaḥ
english: — they all came near, bowing to the ancient grandfather of the worlds. Surrounding the lord of all the worlds, the heavenly ones took their seats.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ manaś ca tejaś cāpy ādadānau divaukasām pūrvadevau vyatikrāntau naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī
english: Drawing away the minds and the radiance of those heavenly ones, the two primal gods, the sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa, passed by.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatiś ca papraccha brāhmaṇaṃ kāv imāv iti bhavantaṃ nopatiṣṭhete tau naḥ śaṃsa pitāmaha
english: Bṛhaspati asked Brahmā, 'Who are these two who do not attend upon you? Tell us about them, O Grandfather.'

sanskrit: brahmovāca yāv etau pṛthivīṃ dyāṃ ca bhāsayantau tapasvinau jvalantau rocamānau ca vyāpyātītau mahābalau
english: Brahmā said: These two who illuminate the earth and the sky, these ascetics, blazing and shining, who have pervaded and transcended all — they are of great might.

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇāv etau lokāl lokaṃ samāsthitau ūrjitau svena tapasā mahāsattvaparākramau
english: These two are Nara and Nārāyaṇa, moving from world to world, vigorous through their own austerity, of great being and valor.

sanskrit: etau hi karmaṇā lokān nandayām āsatur dhruvau asurāṇām abhāvāya devagandharvapūjitau
english: These two, by their deeds, have ever delighted the worlds; they are constant; they are worshipped by gods and gandharvas, and they exist for the destruction of the demons.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca jagāma śakras tac chrutvā yatra tau tepatus tapaḥ sārdhaṃ devagaṇaiḥ sarvair bṛhaspatipurogamaiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, Śakra went to where those two were performing austerities, together with all the hosts of gods headed by Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: tadā devāsure ghore bhaye jāte divaukasām ayācata mahātmānau naranārāyaṇau varam
english: Then, when a terrible fear had arisen for the heavenly ones in the battle between gods and demons, he besought the great-souled Nara and Nārāyaṇa for a boon.

sanskrit: tāv abrūtāṃ vṛṇīṣveti tadā bharatasattama athaitāv abravīc chakraḥ sāhyaṃ naḥ kriyatām iti
english: Those two said, 'Choose.' Then, O best of the Bhāratas, Śakra spoke to those two: 'Let your aid be given to us.'
